new.title: Tour the presidential Château de Rambouillet
new.desc: This former royal, imperial and presidential residence stands in a 980 hectare park inside the forest of Rambouillet. Its calm, remote setting made it a favourite place for diplomacy, and it hosted the first G6 summit in 1975.
new.tip: Trains from Paris Montparnasse run to Rambouillet station, a walk from the château. Check opening days, as it is run by the Centre des monuments nationaux.

new.title: Slip into the Queen's Dairy at Rambouillet
new.desc: Louis XVI had this pleasure dairy built in 1785 for Marie Antoinette, in great secrecy so his money troubles would go unnoticed. A domed rotunda leads to a grotto with a statue of the nymph Amalthea and her goat, one of the great garden follies of the 18th century.
new.tip: It stands near the Bergerie nationale, so see both on one walk. Check seasonal opening times first.

new.title: Marvel at the shell-lined Chaumière aux Coquillages
new.desc: Built around 1770 to 1780 for the Princesse de Lamballe, this thatched cottage looks humble outside. Inside, the main room is richly decorated with marble, shells and mother of pearl, and a smaller room behind hidden doors has painted walls and a mirror.
new.tip: Check the château's website for visit days, as access is limited and seasonal.

new.title: Roll through the miniature trains at Rambolitrain
new.desc: Rambolitrain is a museum of miniature trains in the town of Rambouillet. It makes an easy rainy day stop beside the château quarter.
new.tip: Check opening days before going, as small museums keep limited hours.

new.title: Look for the vanished royal château of Saint-Hubert
new.desc: Louis XV had Ange-Jacques Gabriel build a royal château here in the forest, but it was demolished in 1855 and almost nothing remains. What survives is the woodland setting at Le Perray-en-Yvelines, a reminder of the royal hunts.
new.tip: Combine it with a walk to the Étang de Saint-Hubert. Free access.

new.title: Find the ruined priory at the Rochers d'Angennes
new.desc: The Prieuré Notre-Dame des Moulineaux was a Grandmontine priory that became a seigneurial château in the 18th century, then a pewter factory in the 19th, before being abandoned. Its ruins lie at the place called Rochers d'Angennes in the forest at Poigny-la-Forêt.
new.tip: Wear boots, as forest tracks can be muddy. Free to explore.

new.title: Climb to the medieval Château de la Madeleine
new.desc: A well preserved medieval fortress that looks down over Chevreuse and its valley. It belongs to the Yvelines department and houses the headquarters of the Haute Vallée de Chevreuse regional nature park.
new.tip: Walk up from the town for the valley views. Check opening times if you want to go inside the park offices and grounds.

new.title: Meet the wax figures at the Château de Breteuil
new.desc: This château at Choisel in the Chevreuse valley shows scenes from the life and history of the estate, staged with wax figures made by the Musée Grévin and automata by Janie and Armand Langlois. It is a lively family stop in a protected park setting.
new.tip: Allow half a day for house and grounds. Check seasonal opening before you go.

new.title: Wander the Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay
new.desc: A Cistercian monastery from the 12th century, set in the forest of Rambouillet in the Chevreuse valley and inside the regional nature park. It became a hotel in 1988 and was listed as a historic monument in 1994.
new.tip: Walk the grounds and the valley around it. Weekdays are quiet.

new.title: Walk the quiet valley of Port-Royal des Champs
new.desc: Port-Royal des Champs was an abbey of Cistercian nuns in the Chevreuse valley that launched a number of culturally important institutions. A national museum now stands on the site of the abbey and the old Granges farm.
new.tip: Check the museum's opening days. The grounds are lovely for a stroll.

new.title: Visit the Renaissance Château de Thoiry
new.desc: A Renaissance château at Thoiry, on an estate of 380 hectares that also holds the safari park. It sits in rural western Yvelines, about 50 km from Paris.
new.tip: Combined tickets with the safari park are usually available. Check opening times.

new.title: Step inside Maurice Ravel's house at Montfort-l'Amaury
new.desc: Ravel lived at Le Belvédère, below the castle ruins, from 1921 until 1937. The house opened as a museum in 1973 and is run by the town.
new.tip: Visits are usually guided, so book ahead and check opening days.

new.title: Count the Renaissance windows of Montfort's church
new.desc: The Église Saint-Pierre was rebuilt in 1491 under Anne de Bretagne and holds 37 Renaissance stained glass windows from the later 16th century, described as unique in the Île-de-France. It has been a historic monument since 1840.
new.tip: Entry is free. Take time to look at the glass in good daylight.

new.title: Climb to the Anne-de-Bretagne tower in Montfort
new.desc: The Tour Anne-de-Bretagne is a 15th century tower perched on the feudal mound that rises over the village. It is the main remnant of the old castle, whose ruins have been classified as a historic monument.
new.tip: Walk up from the village centre. Combine it with Ravel's house just below.

new.title: Visit Jean Monnet's house at Houjarray
new.desc: Jean Monnet, one of the architects of European unity, lived in this house from 1945 until his death in 1979. It stands in the hamlet of Houjarray near Montfort-l'Amaury, on the rue du Vieux Pressoir.
new.tip: Visits depend on opening days, so check ahead.
new.q: Maison de Jean Monnet, Houjarray, Bazoches-sur-Guyonne

new.title: Climb the Donjon de Houdan
new.desc: Built by Amaury III de Montfort, this massive tower of about 25 metres has four turrets and is one of the last remains of the town's fortifications. From 1880 to 1970 it served as a water reservoir, and it is now a museum.
new.tip: Check opening times if you want to go inside. Seen from outside it is free.

new.title: Admire Houdan's Gothic church with its Renaissance choir
new.desc: The Église Saint-Jacques and Saint-Christophe dates from the 15th and 16th centuries, mixing Gothic style with a Renaissance choir. It is listed as a historic monument.
new.tip: Entry is usually free. Pair it with the keep and the old timber houses.

new.title: Spot the half-timbered Hôtel du Lys in Houdan
new.desc: This timber framed building on the rue de Paris dates from the late 15th century. It is one of the best preserved medieval houses in Houdan's old centre.
new.tip: Free to see from the street. Combine with the keep and church.
new.q: Hôtel du Lys, 64 rue de Paris, Houdan

new.title: Tour François Mansart's château at Maisons-Laffitte
new.desc: Designed by François Mansart between 1630 and 1651, this château is a masterpiece of 17th century civil architecture and marks the shift from late Renaissance to classicism. The banker Jacques Laffitte later owned it and gave the town its name.
new.tip: Check opening days. Combine it with a stroll through the horse-loving town.

new.title: Visit Le Corbusier's white box, Villa Savoye
new.desc: Built from 1928 to 1931 by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret, the villa is a white block on thin pilotis with ribbon windows and roof terraces. It is part of the group of Le Corbusier works on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
new.tip: Check opening days. It is a short walk or bus ride from Poissy station.
new.q: Villa Savoye, 82 rue de Villiers, Poissy

new.title: Find Saint Louis's baptismal font in Poissy
new.desc: The Collégiale Notre-Dame was founded around 1016 by King Robert the Pious, and the future Louis IX was baptised here days after his birth in Poissy in 1214. The font of that time is still kept in the church.
new.tip: Entry is usually free. The toy museum is a few steps away.

new.title: Play at the toy museum in Poissy's priory gate
new.desc: The Musée du Jouet occupies the gatehouse, the only surviving part of the Dominican priory of Saint-Louis that was almost entirely destroyed in the Revolution. It is a fun stop for families.
new.tip: Check opening times, as the museum keeps limited days.

new.title: Stand at the watering trough Sisley painted
new.desc: The Abreuvoir de Marly is one of two elements that survive from Louis XIV's gardens at Marly. Alfred Sisley painted it at Marly-le-Roi in 1876 and it became a favourite subject of his Marly series.
new.tip: Free to see. Continue into the royal estate afterwards.

new.title: Browse the museum of the royal Domaine de Marly
new.desc: The Musée du domaine royal de Marly shows archaeological finds from Louis XIV's lost château. It is run jointly by the towns of Marly-le-Roi and Louveciennes.
new.tip: Check opening days before you go.
new.q: Musée du Domaine royal de Marly, Marly-le-Roi

new.title: Look up at the Louveciennes aqueduct
new.desc: A 17th century aqueduct built under Louis XIV as part of the hydraulic system that brought Seine water to the gardens of Marly and Versailles. It is out of service today and has been listed as a historic monument since 1953.
new.tip: Walk the path beneath it. Free to view.

new.title: Trace the Machine de Marly in Bougival
new.desc: Built between 1681 and 1688 by Rennequin Sualem, this vast Seine pumping system fed the gardens of Marly and Versailles. It ran for 133 years before being replaced by later pumps, with electric pumps taking over in 1968.
new.tip: Read the history boards and walk the riverbank. Check access.

new.title: Admire Madame du Barry's music pavilion
new.desc: The pavilion de musique, built by Claude Nicolas Ledoux, is the reception pavilion of Madame du Barry's château at Louveciennes. The château itself was built by Robert de Cotte and later redecorated for her, and the estate has been listed since 1994.
new.tip: It is best seen from public paths. Check open days.
new.q: Pavillon de musique de Madame du Barry, Louveciennes

new.title: Visit the Turgenev museum at Bougival
new.desc: The Musée Ivan-Tourgueniev stands at 16 rue Yvan Tourgueneff in Bougival. It is currently reached only through the forest car park on rue de la Croix aux Vents.
new.tip: Check opening days and the access route before you go.
new.q: Musée Ivan-Tourgueniev, 16 rue Yvan Tourgueneff, Bougival

new.title: Lunch where Renoir painted at Maison Fournaise
new.desc: The Maison Fournaise is a former guinguette and hotel on the Île des Impressionnistes, best known as a place where Renoir painted. Today it houses both a restaurant and the town museum on the history of the site and of boating.
new.tip: Book a table if you want lunch. Museum opening days vary.

new.title: Walk the Île des Impressionnistes
new.desc: This island on the Seine between Chatou and Rueil was a playground of the Impressionists and today holds the Fournaise hamlet and a research centre. It was originally two islands joined by a dyke.
new.tip: Free to walk. Bring a picnic for the river views.

new.title: Hunt for bargains at the Chatou antiques and ham fair
new.desc: The Foire nationale à la brocante et aux jambons has been held twice a year on the Île des Impressionnistes since 1970. About 800 antique dealers set up alongside stands selling hams, charcuterie and regional specialities.
new.tip: Check the dates of the two yearly editions before you go, and arrive early for the best finds.
new.q: Foire de Chatou, Île des Impressionnistes, Chatou

new.title: Cross the Pont de Chatou over the Seine
new.desc: The Pont de Chatou links Chatou and Rueil-Malmaison and is the latest in a line of bridges at this spot. The current one dates from 1966.
new.tip: Walk across for views of the river and the island.

new.title: Find the site of La Grenouillère at Croissy
new.desc: La Grenouillère was a famous boating, bathing, dancing and dining establishment on an island at Croissy-sur-Seine, open from 1850 to 1920. A local museum on the Grande Rue keeps its memory alive.
new.tip: Check the museum's opening days before you go.
new.q: Musée de la Grenouillère, Grande Rue, Croissy-sur-Seine

new.title: Admire Mantes' Notre-Dame look-alike
new.desc: The collegiate church of Notre-Dame was built in the 12th and 13th centuries beside the Seine and recalls Paris's Notre-Dame in style and its three level elevation. It was listed as a historic monument in 1840.
new.tip: Entry is usually free. The riverside is a short walk away.

new.title: Browse the Musée de l'Hôtel-Dieu in Mantes
new.desc: The museum sits on the Impressionists' road in the former medieval chapel of the Hôtel-Dieu, whose classical façade is a listed monument. It reopened after a major renovation of its spaces and collections.
new.tip: Check opening days. It is close to the collegiate church.

new.title: Find the Saint-Maclou tower in Mantes
new.desc: The Tour Saint-Maclou is all that remains of one of Mantes' former parish churches. It has been a listed monument since 1908.
new.tip: Free to see. Combine it with the collegiate church.

new.title: Cross one of France's oldest bridges at Limay
new.desc: The Vieux pont de Limay spans an arm of the Seine to join Limay to the Île aux Dames and is counted among the oldest bridges in France. It looks across to Mantes.
new.tip: Walk over for river views. Free.

new.title: Spot the Château des Célestins in Limay
new.desc: This neoclassical château in Limay was built on the site of the Célestins monastery of the Holy Trinity, which was suppressed in 1778. It is a quiet piece of Seine valley heritage.
new.tip: Check whether grounds are open before you go.

new.title: Visit Émile Zola's house at Médan
new.desc: Zola's house at 26 rue Pasteur in Médan reopened to visitors after works and can only be visited on a guided tour. Zola was the leading figure of naturalism and a key defender of Alfred Dreyfus.
new.tip: Book the guided visit in advance and check opening days.
new.q: Maison d'Émile Zola, 26 rue Pasteur, Médan

new.title: Learn river lore at the Musée de la Batellerie
new.desc: Conflans-Sainte-Honorine is the main French town of inland navigation, and its museum of the barge trade is housed in the Château du Prieuré. It tells the story of life on the Seine and Oise.
new.tip: Check opening days. Walk down to the quays afterwards.
new.q: Musée de la Batellerie, Château du Prieuré, Conflans-Sainte-Honorine

new.title: Climb to the medieval Tour Montjoie in Conflans
new.desc: The Tour Montjoie is a medieval tower in the old upper town of Conflans-Sainte-Honorine. The lanes around it give views down to the river.
new.tip: Free to see from outside. Wear good shoes for the climb.

new.title: See the Eiffel bridge over the Oise at Conflans
new.desc: The Pont Eiffel is a double track railway bridge carrying the Paris Saint-Lazare to Mantes line across the Oise between Conflans-Sainte-Honorine and Andrésy. It is an industrial landmark of the confluence.
new.tip: View it from the riverbanks. Free.

new.title: Cross the suspension bridge at Triel-sur-Seine
new.desc: The Pont suspendu de Triel carries a road over the Seine. The present bridge opened in 1956 and replaced the first suspension bridge on the site.
new.tip: Walk across and look along the river. Free.

new.title: Wander Triel's big church with four eras
new.desc: Saint-Martin in Triel-sur-Seine is a vast church built in four different periods, from a Gothic nave of the 12th century to later extensions of the late 15th and mid 16th centuries. The plan became very complex as it grew.
new.tip: Entry is usually free.

new.title: Climb the highest point of the Île-de-France
new.desc: The Colline d'Élancourt rises 231 metres and is entirely artificial, built from waste and fill. From the top you can see the Eiffel Tower, the Montparnasse tower and La Défense, and it hosted the mountain bike events of the 2024 Olympics.
new.tip: Free. Go on a clear day for the views.

new.title: Explore the Musée de la ville de Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines
new.desc: The museum is a Musée de France with a collection of more than 6000 objects, telling the story of the new town and its society. It is run by the Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines agglomeration.
new.tip: Check opening days before you go.
new.q: Musée de la ville de Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines

new.title: See printed cotton at the Musée de la Toile de Jouy
new.desc: Toile de Jouy is a cotton cloth printed with figures and scenes, usually in a single colour such as red or aubergine on a cream ground. The municipal museum, created in 1977, is in the Château de l'Églantine at Jouy-en-Josas.
new.tip: Check opening times before you go.
new.q: Musée de la Toile de Jouy, Jouy-en-Josas

new.title: Visit Léon Blum's home at Jouy-en-Josas
new.desc: The former prime minister Léon Blum lived in this house for five years and died here on 30 March 1950. The property has a heritage label for houses of illustrious people.
new.tip: Check whether visits are open before you go.
new.q: Maison de Léon et Jeanne Blum, Jouy-en-Josas

new.title: Discover the Fondation de Coubertin
new.desc: The Fondation de Coubertin aims to improve the professional, intellectual and cultural training of young people from manual trades, passing on values of quality and honesty in work. It sits in the Chevreuse valley at Saint-Rémy-lès-Chevreuse.
new.tip: Check visit days, as access is limited.

new.title: Visit the home of Elsa Triolet and Aragon
new.desc: Elsa Triolet, the first woman to win the Goncourt prize, was married to the poet Louis Aragon and died at Saint-Arnoult-en-Yvelines in 1970. Their house here, the Moulin de Villeneuve, is now a museum.
new.tip: Check opening days and reserve if needed.
new.q: Maison Elsa Triolet-Aragon, Moulin de Villeneuve, Saint-Arnoult-en-Yvelines

new.title: Seek the abbey ruins of Joyenval on the golf course
new.desc: The Abbaye de Joyenval was a Premonstratensian abbey whose remains now lie on a golf course at the edge of the Marly forest, near the Désert de Retz at Chambourcy. It is an unusual mix of monastic ruin and fairway.
new.tip: Check access, as the site is within a golf estate.

new.title: Meet the merino sheep at the Bergerie nationale
new.desc: Louis XVI founded this experimental farm in 1785 with a Merino flock bought from the King of Spain, the ancestors of the Rambouillet Merino breed. Today a visitor circuit lets you see dairy and beef cows, draft horses, goats and poultry, and a small sheep museum is on site.
new.tip: Combine it with the Laiterie de la Reine. Good for children, and the farm shop is a good place for local produce.
new.q: Bergerie nationale, Parc du Château, Rambouillet

new.title: Walk the shore of the Étang d'Or in Rambouillet forest
new.desc: The forest of Rambouillet covers 200 square kilometres and is dotted with ponds, rocky areas, sandy stretches, valleys and waterfalls. Oak makes up 68 percent of its trees. The Étang d'Or is one of its ponds.
new.tip: Weekday mornings are quietest. Bring water and a map.
new.q: Étang d'Or, forêt de Rambouillet, Rambouillet

new.title: Circle the Étang de Saint-Hubert at sunrise
new.desc: The Étang de Saint-Hubert lies in the forest of Rambouillet near the lost royal château of the same name. Woodland paths loop around the water.
new.tip: Go early for mist and wildlife. Park near the pond and follow the paths.

new.title: Explore the Louis XIV ponds of the Étangs de Hollande
new.desc: These ponds are artificial, created in the late 17th century under Louis XIV to collect water from the Rambouillet plateau and help feed the fountains of the Versailles park. They now make a quiet woodland walk near Saint-Léger-en-Yvelines.
new.tip: Stay on marked paths. Spring is good for birdsong.

new.title: Visit the zoological reserve at the Château de Sauvage
new.desc: The Réserve zoologique de Sauvage lies in the 36 hectare park of the Château de Sauvage at Émancé, about 12 km south west of Rambouillet. The park was acquired in 1973 for animal conservation.
new.tip: Check opening dates and book ahead if required.

new.title: Walk to the Étangs de Bonnelles nature reserve
new.desc: The Réserve naturelle régionale des étangs de Bonnelles covers 22 hectares of ponds and wetland. It was first classified in 1990 and reclassified as a regional reserve in 2016.
new.tip: Stay on paths and respect reserve rules. Check access points before you go.
new.q: Réserve naturelle des Étangs de Bonnelles, Bonnelles

new.title: Watch birds in the Boucle de Moisson reserve
new.desc: The Réserve naturelle régionale de la boucle de Moisson protects 316 hectares inside a meander of the Seine. It was classified in 2009.
new.tip: Bring binoculars and check access rules before you go.
new.q: Réserve naturelle de la Boucle de Moisson, Moisson

new.title: Stroll the horse capital of Maisons-Laffitte
new.desc: Maisons-Laffitte is nicknamed the city of the horse because of its large equestrian activity. Its parkland streets are lined with stables, so you may meet horses on their morning exercise.
new.tip: Go in the morning and respect the working areas.

new.title: Stroll the Parc de la boucle de Montesson
new.desc: This departmental park on the Seine at Montesson was laid out by the Yvelines council from 1997 in the former Borde estate, bought in 1992. It is a riverside green space for walks and picnics.
new.tip: Free to enter. Bring a picnic.
new.q: Parc départemental de la boucle de Montesson, Montesson

new.title: Walk the Île de Migneaux on the Seine
new.desc: The Île de Migneaux is a Seine island about 2.5 km long but less than 100 metres wide between Poissy and Carrières-sous-Poissy. A 1933 bow-string road bridge links it to Poissy, and roughly 400 people live on it in about a hundred houses.
new.tip: Walk or cycle the length of the island. Free.

new.title: Spot birds in the Parc du Peuple de l'herbe
new.desc: A 113 hectare departmental park in Carrières-sous-Poissy, open to the public since 2016, set up to safeguard water birds, insects and plants.
new.tip: Bring binoculars and check access hours before you go.
new.q: Parc du Peuple de l'herbe, Carrières-sous-Poissy

new.title: Trace the lost château in the Domaine de Marly
new.desc: Louis XIV commissioned the Château de Marly in 1679 as a retreat for invited guests, but it was sold in 1799 and dismantled. The park survives, with the Grand Miroir basin and the watering trough from the original gardens.
new.tip: Free to walk. Look for the outline of the royal pavilion on the ground.

new.title: Walk the long Île de la Loge
new.desc: The Île de la Loge is a Seine island about 2.5 km long between Le Port-Marly, Louveciennes, Bougival and Croissy-sur-Seine. A road bridge and a footbridge link it to the left bank.
new.tip: Follow the riverside paths. Free.

new.title: Shrink France at France Miniature
new.desc: A miniature park at Élancourt, opened in May 1991, with 117 French monuments and sites reproduced at 1:30 scale. A tour of France in an afternoon.
new.tip: Best in good weather. Check the opening season.

new.title: Walk the shore of the Étang de Saint-Quentin
new.desc: The Étang de Saint-Quentin is the largest body of water in the Île-de-France and sits inside a big leisure base in the new town of Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines. Paths run around it.
new.tip: Check what activities are open that day.
new.q: Île de loisirs de Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines, Trappes

new.title: See the Golf National that hosted Olympic golf
new.desc: Le Golf National at Guyancourt hosted the Olympic golf tournaments of the 2024 Games, with 60 men and 60 women over four rounds each. It is a rare chance to play where the Olympians did.
new.tip: Check the club's site for public tee times.

new.title: Drive through the wildlife reserve at Thoiry
new.desc: Opened in 1968 as the Réserve africaine de Thoiry, the safari park now covers 150 of the estate's 380 hectares and holds about 1500 animals, including roughly 95 species of mammals.
new.tip: Book ahead in school holidays and arrive early.

new.title: Taste the original Paris-Brest at Pâtisserie Durand
new.desc: Louis Durand created the Paris-Brest at this pâtisserie in 1910 to mark a cycling race, and the family has kept the recipe secret since. It is a wheel of choux pastry topped with almonds and filled with praline cream.
new.tip: Typically open daily except Monday. Take it to the château park nearby.
new.q: Pâtisserie Durand, 9 avenue de Longueil, Maisons-Laffitte

new.title: Try the sourdough at Boulangerie L'Héritage
new.desc: This Maisons-Laffitte bakery is known for its long-fermented sourdough bread and is listed by Gault&Millau. It is one of the best addresses in the town's rich bakery scene.
new.tip: Go early for the freshest loaves.
new.q: Boulangerie L'Héritage, 2 rue George V, Maisons-Laffitte

new.title: Share a Lebanese meze at Boulevard Beirut in Poissy
new.desc: A Lebanese restaurant in Poissy located between the Collégiale Notre-Dame and the old bridge. It is a handy place to eat after seeing the town's sights.
new.tip: Book at weekends and check opening days.
new.q: Boulevard Beirut, 5 avenue Maurice Berteaux, Poissy

new.title: Order a galette at Crêperie Cavrosa near Chevreuse
new.desc: A Breton style crêperie in a former coaching inn between Le Mesnil-Saint-Denis and Saint-Rémy-lès-Chevreuse, using flour from the Ferme de la Budinerie and mostly organic produce. Farm cider is on the drinks list and the room has exposed beams and a central fireplace.
new.tip: It is often full, so book ahead. There is free parking.
new.q: Crêperie Cavrosa, Route de Versailles, Le Mesnil-Saint-Denis

new.title: Taste organic Volcelest beer at the Chevreuse brewery
new.desc: The Brasserie de la Vallée de Chevreuse at Le Perray-en-Yvelines brews organic beers under the Volcelest name, from blond and white to amber, IPA and stout, plus two seasonal beers. Gault&Millau lists it among artisan producers.
new.tip: Check click and collect or shop opening before you go.
new.q: Brasserie de la Vallée de Chevreuse, 28 rue du Roseau, Le Perray-en-Yvelines

new.title: Sip a craft beer from La Barge in Rambouillet
new.desc: La Barge is a Rambouillet brewery listed by the local tourist office among the producers of the Rambouillet territories. It sits on the rue de Clairefontaine.
new.tip: Check how to buy before you go, as small breweries keep limited hours.
new.q: La Barge, 23 rue de Clairefontaine, Rambouillet

new.title: Buy farm goods at the Ferme de la Villeneuve
new.desc: A Rambouillet farm listed by the tourist office for honey, fruit, vegetables, poultry and cheese. It sits on the rue du Champ de Course.
new.tip: Check opening times before you go.
new.q: Ferme de la Villeneuve, 60 rue du Champ de Course, Rambouillet

new.title: Taste cheese at the Ferme de la Tremblaye
new.desc: A farm at La Boissière-École listed by the Rambouillet tourist office for its cheese. It is a good stop on a countryside drive west of Rambouillet.
new.tip: Check shop opening before you go.
new.q: Ferme de la Tremblaye, La Boissière-École

new.title: Meet the goats at the Chèvrerie de Vilpert
new.desc: A goat farm at Poigny-la-Forêt on the route de Saint-Léger, listed by the Rambouillet tourist office. Its cheeses are sold directly.
new.tip: Check opening before you go.
new.q: Chèvrerie de Vilpert, 65 route de Saint-Léger, Poigny-la-Forêt

new.title: Taste sparkling apple juice at the Ferme de Louareux
new.desc: This Sonchamp farm works with apples and sells sparkling apple, apple juice, jams, caramel and jelly. Free apple picking runs from mid August to the end of October.
new.tip: It is listed as open every day. Check the picking days if you want to pick.
new.q: Ferme de Louareux, Hameau de Louareux, Sonchamp

new.title: Shop for honey and beer at the Ferme des Clos
new.desc: The Ferme des Clos at Bonnelles is listed by the Rambouillet tourist office for honey, fruit, vegetables and beer.
new.tip: Check opening before you go.
new.q: Ferme des Clos, Chemin des Clos, Bonnelles

new.title: Buy farm cheese and honey at the Ferme de la Noue
new.desc: A farm at La Celle-les-Bordes listed by the Rambouillet tourist office for fruit, vegetables, honey and cheese.
new.tip: Check opening before you go.
new.q: Ferme de la Noue, La Celle-les-Bordes

new.title: Dine on the terrace at Le Coq de Bougival
new.desc: A restaurant in a historic building on the quai Rennequin-Sualem at Bougival, serving generous traditional cooking with a large summer terrace.
new.tip: Book for summer weekends.
new.q: Le Coq de Bougival, Quai Rennequin-Sualem, Bougival

new.title: Eat on the Seine terrace at La Casa in Médan
new.desc: A bistronomic brasserie with cocktails and an extra large terrace on the Seine, in a historic building linked to Émile Zola.
new.tip: Combine with a visit to Zola's house. Book for weekends.
new.q: La Casa, Quai de Seine, Médan

new.title: Lunch at the Auberge des 3 Hameaux near Breteuil
new.desc: An inn with bistronomic cooking in the Chevreuse valley, close to the Château de Breteuil at Choisel, with a leafy terrace.
new.tip: Book ahead, especially at weekends.
new.q: Auberge des 3 Hameaux, 2 rue de la Maison Forte, Choisel

new.title: Dine at La Parenthèse Verte in Louveciennes
new.desc: A bistronomic restaurant set in a green park with a terrace, in Louveciennes on the rue de la Princesse.
new.tip: Book ahead and ask about the terrace.
new.q: La Parenthèse Verte, rue de la Princesse, Louveciennes

new.title: Eat by the river at La Maison Louveciennes
new.desc: A festive bistronomic restaurant on the quai Conti at Louveciennes with a summer beach on the Seine, about 20 minutes from Paris.
new.tip: Best in summer. Book at weekends.
new.q: La Maison Louveciennes, Quai Conti, Louveciennes

new.title: Settle in at the Bistrot des Tours in Montfort
new.desc: A bistro on the place de la Libération in Montfort-l'Amaury, rated 4.4 out of 5 by diners on Petit Futé. A good lunch stop after the village's sights.
new.tip: Book at weekends.
new.q: Bistrot des Tours, 5 place de la Libération, Montfort-l'Amaury

new.title: Taste the poule de Houdan and its pâté
new.desc: The Houdan hen is a black, white-speckled breed with a big crest and five toes, prized before 1914 and revived by a breeders' club in 1979, and now holds a Label Rouge. A local brotherhood celebrates the bird and the pâté de Houdan, a pâté en croûte.
new.tip: Ask for local poultry or pâté at the town's shops and restaurants.

new.title: Join the Foire Saint-Matthieu in Houdan
new.desc: Houdan's Foire Saint-Matthieu is held the last weekend of September and dates back to 1065, making it one of Europe's oldest fairs. In 1777 Louis XVI extended it to several days.
new.tip: Check the dates for the last weekend of September.
